entry.title: MLB: What to watch on September 12, 2026
entry.content:

  • Pitcher 'no data': Pitchers only have a pNERD score once they've started at least one game and have at least 20 innings pitched. I also show 'no data' when I can't correctly link a starting pitcher with their stats.
  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

Paul Skenes still owns the game's watchability, even though his season line hasn't matched his Cy Young-caliber ceiling, and this Cubs-Pirates rubber match carries real playoff stakes for Chicago. This is the highest gNERD score on the board today (16.09 against a 7.44–16.09 range), driven mostly by an excellent Cubs team and a dominant arm. Skenes brings a 9.80 pNERD - elite by any measure, powered by plus velocity, a hefty swinging-strike rate, and youth on his side - though he's been homer prone. He's struggled in two starts versus the Cubs this season, going 0-2 with a 5.06 ERA, and is 2-4 with a 3.45 ERA in nine career appearances against Chicago, so there's a real revenge-game angle here. Clay Holmes (4.99 pNERD) is comparatively pedestrian but serviceable, and he's been Chicago's steadiest arm all September. The Cubs' 10.36 tNERD is elite - built on standout batting and fielding runs - while Pittsburgh's roster is dealing with injuries to Braxton Ashcraft, Mitch Keller, Endy Rodríguez, Kirby Yates, and now outfielder Esmerlyn Valdez. Add in Alex Bregman's two-run homer and near-cycle in Friday's 12-2 win, his 25th of the season, and you've got a marquee arm facing a hot lineup with something to prove on both sides.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

A dominant Dodgers ace against a fading Marlins club still makes for a solid watch, mostly thanks to Tyler Glasnow's clean stuff. Glasnow is 4-0 with a 3.12 ERA and 10.9 strikeouts per nine innings in his return from the injured list, and this is his fourth start since returning from the injured list—he's been especially sharp against Miami specifically, 2-0 with a 1.59 ERA in three career starts at loanDepot park. His pNERD of 8.83 is well above average, built on elite xFIP- and above-average velocity and whiff rates. Phillips, by contrast, is a league-average arm who started the season in the bullpen but since joining the rotation has a 4.23 ERA and 4.91 xERA in 17 starts—his 4.95 pNERD reflects that mediocrity, though his underlying stuff isn't bad. The Dodgers arrive at 90-57 and lead the National League West, while Miami has lost four in a row. Miami's tNERD (9.00) actually edges LA's (7.90), fueled by a young, cheap roster outperforming its underlying batted-ball data—positive regression could be coming. Combined 15.34 gNERD sits near the top of today's slate, and comfortably above the historical average, making this an easy recommend if you like watching a real ace work.

New York Mets @ New York Yankees, 10:35a

Summary

Subway Series drama with a lopsided pitching résumé — Cole’s stuff against a Mets club still mathematically clinging to October, though barely. Worth a look for the rivalry and Juan Soto's return to the Bronx alone, even if the on-paper mismatch is real.

The Yankees own the better team NERD here (8.13 vs. 5.71), riding an excellent barrel rate and solid all-around performance in front of home fans on a six-game winning streak. The Mets counter with better bullpen work and barrel rate of their own, but overall are the weaker side, and their four-game winning streak sounds like momentum until you look at how thin the lineup gets outside the top of the order. Soto has been terrific in the middle at .274 with 24 homers and a .918 OPS since returning from the injured list in late August, giving the Mets at least one reason to tune in.

On the mound, Cole is the story: at 35 he's still humming, sitting near 97 mph with elite strike-throwing, and his 7.26 pNERD ranks well above today's average. That said, his recent form is softer — he has allowed 11 earned runs over his last four starts, a span of 24.1 innings, with only 21 strikeouts, and oddly he has never solved this opponent, owning a 6.99 ERA against the Mets across nine career starts. Opposite him, rookie Zac Thornton has no NERD data available, and is coming off a rough outing where he gave up six earned runs on seven hits, including four home runs, across five innings in a loss to the Giants. The 13.05 gNERD sits comfortably above the historical median and roughly in line with today's average, making this a moderately watchable game elevated mainly by the rivalry and Cole's track record rather than raw upside on both sides.

Chicago White Sox @ St. Louis Cardinals, 4:15p

Summary

A tepid matchup between two teams playing out the string, though the gNERD score of 12.78 sits comfortably above average and there's just enough spice to make it watchable. Both clubs are far from contention — the White Sox at 75-71 have dropped nine of their last twelve, while the Cardinals (73-75) just snapped a three-game skid behind rookies Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal, who each finished with three hits and two RBIs in a 7-3 win Friday. Jordan Walker keeps the Cardinals lineup interesting, while Munetaka Murakami's power bat gives Chicago a puncher's chance in any at-bat. On the mound, Kyle Leahy is the more intriguing arm, his 87 xFIP- driving a solid 5.65 pNERD, while Sean Newcomb's 5.55 pNERD comes more from a plodding pace than swing-and-miss stuff. Team-wise, Chicago's young, cost-controlled roster (8.43 tNERD) outshines St. Louis's more middling profile (5.94 tNERD), though both squads carry some bad-luck underperformance that suggests better days could be ahead. Not a marquee game, but a solid one for a lazy afternoon.

Cincinnati Reds @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:10p

Summary

Milwaukee mashes, Cincinnati flails, and the "TBD" starter turns out to be Kyle Harrison, who's been nearly untouchable at home — this one's more one-sided rout than nail-biter.

The Brewers, sitting 10 games up in the NL Central, have won nine of their last ten at home and just finished torching Cincinnati 20-0 the night before. Their offense backs it up statistically — Milwaukee's tNERD of 10.04 is elite, built on strong batting runs, baserunning, and a bullpen that's been quietly excellent all year. Cincinnati, by contrast, limps in with four straight losses and a lineup that's cratered — hitting .230 over its past 29 games with a .305 on-base percentage. That's reflected in their middling 4.61 tNERD, propped up mostly by a young, cheap roster and some positive batting luck that suggests better days ahead, eventually.

On the mound, Brady Singer brings a modest 4.31 pNERD, and the surface stats haven't been kind either — he's allowed at least three earned runs in nine consecutive starts. Kyle Harrison, meanwhile, has been dominant at American Family Field, posting a 1.26 ERA and 0.84 WHIP across 11 home starts, though we have no NERD data on him. The 11.98 gNERD sits right around today's average, so watch if you like lopsided baseball with a hot team stomping a cold one.

Cleveland Guardians @ Minnesota Twins, 1:10p

Summary

A playoff-race afternoon featuring a fireballing Cleveland reclamation project against a hard-throwing Twins rookie who's quietly been one of the better arms in baseball this year. Daniel Espino's story alone makes this worth a look: the 2019 first-rounder dealt with several major shoulder injuries that derailed his climb through the minors before finally reaching the majors in June, and he's still been regularly hitting at least 99 mph with his fastball, even reaching back for 100.6 mph. We don't have reliable statistical projections for him yet (pNERD sits at zero), so his outing is pure watch-and-see. On the other side, Connor Prielipp brings real substance — a 7.80 pNERD built on a sharp xFIP-, mid-90s velocity, and youth, though his shiny 34.0 luck figure suggests his results have been running well ahead of his peripherals and some regression could be coming. Cleveland's tNERD (6.79) outpaces Minnesota's (3.03), largely thanks to Guardians' bullpen strength, youth, and modest payroll versus a Twins group that's been shaky on the bases and in the field. At 11.31, the gNERD lands almost exactly at today's average, but Espino's stuff and backstory make it more interesting than the number alone suggests.

San Diego Padres @ San Francisco Giants, 1:05p

Summary

Padres vs. Giants offers a real contrast: a surging playoff contender with a bullpen for the ages against a last-place club clinging to a promising young arm's early magic. San Diego brings a five-game winning streak and the majors' best bullpen by our numbers, while Michael King has been dealing since July, going 5-2 with a 2.26 ERA over his last twelve starts. He's not overpowering by the underlying metrics — his pNERD sits below average, dragged down by middling strikeout and walk rates — but he's a reliable frontline arm in a real NL West scrap. The bigger novelty is on the other side: rookie lefty Cesar Perdomo, making just his second big-league start after firing six scoreless innings in his debut against the Mets, tries to back up a 0.90 ERA with almost no MLB track record (hence the blank pNERD — the data simply isn't there yet). San Francisco's tNERD is thin, weighed down by weak baserunning and fielding, though a bit of negative luck suggests some in-season overperformance could regress. Overall gNERD lands at 11.15, just above the historical average and squarely mid-pack among today's slate — watchable mostly for the standings stakes and Perdomo's small sample intrigue.

Los Angeles Angels @ Washington Nationals, 1:05p

Summary

Two also-rans playing out the string meet in Washington, but the pitching matchup and the Nationals' late-inning theatrics make this more watchable than the standings suggest. The Nationals snapped a seven-game losing streak Friday on Jorbit Vivas' tiebreaking two-run double in the eighth, and Washington's tNERD (8.26) reflects a genuinely lively young offense — strong baserunning and barrel rates — dragged down almost entirely by a bullpen that's been a disaster (bullpen runs z-score of -2.23). The Angels, by contrast, are close to replacement-level across the board, their 0.85 tNERD a testament to bad batting, baserunning, and fielding all at once. The real draw is 22-year-old rookie Walbert Ureña, who's quietly been excellent: 9-10, posting a 2.74 ERA, 124 strikeouts across 131.1 innings, and a 1.21 WHIP, last taking the mound against the Pittsburgh Pirates and surrendering one earned run over eight innings. His 98 mph heat drives a 7.50 pNERD, though his control can wobble — he once needed 3.2 innings to issue five free passes against Cleveland. Andrew Alvarez, with a tidy xFIP-, is a solid if unspectacular opposite number. Overall, a middling gNERD (10.86) that's carried more by curiosity about Ureña than by anything the standings promise.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Good, this gave enough. Now write the summary.

A pennant race in late September with a scrambling Phillies rotation makes this one worth a look, even if the pure NERD math is middling. The Braves hold a lead atop the NL East, and Philadelphia is scrapping to keep pace, having just dropped a marathon 11-inning series opener that ran past 11 p.m.

The Phillies lost 6-5 in 11 innings in the series opener, a game that went on until 11 p.m. because of a rain delay. Making matters worse for Philadelphia, expected starter Jesús Luzardo was scratched due to shoulder soreness, and their typical spot starter had already pitched two days prior, leaving the Phillies scrambling to find a starter — hence the TBD, which drags the pitching side of this gNERD down to zero for that half of the matchup. On the other side, Tyler Mahle brings real intrigue: he's been sharp since arriving in Atlanta at the Trade Deadline, posting a 1.24 ERA in six starts after a rough 5.13 ERA in 18 starts with the Giants, and his xFIP- of 91 backs up that a strong finish is real, not just luck. Atlanta's bullpen and barrel rate give them a modest offensive/defensive edge on paper, and with the Braves having won this season series decisively, the Phillies badly need value from wherever their bullpen game can find it. Today's gNERD sits below average, but the stakes make it worth a look.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

This one's near the top of the board today, thanks largely to a Cubs offense and defense that's humming and a pitching mismatch that's more interesting than it looks on paper. Chicago's Shota Imanaga takes a full week of rest into this one and has flat-out owned Pittsburgh this year — he has dominated the Pirates twice this season with a combined 12 scoreless innings, 13 strikeouts, two walks, and just four hits. His whiff rate and contact-suppression numbers back it up, giving him a solid pNERD score even if his home-run rate has been a season-long headache. Opposite him: Wilber Dotel, who is making his first big-league start in place of injured All-Star Braxton Ashcraft, after pitching out of the bullpen all season — an unknown-stats zero on the pNERD ledger, essentially a bullpen game for Pittsburgh. The Cubs' tNERD is elite, powered by top-shelf batting and fielding runs, offset only by a shaky bullpen; Pittsburgh counters with strong baserunning but leaky defense. Combined, this gNERD checks in comfortably above the historical average and leads the day's slate — worth tuning in, especially to see if Dotel can hang with a rested Imanaga.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Miami Marlins, 4:10p

Summary

A near-average matchup on paper turns intriguing once you clock who's actually walking to the mound. Padres are still in the thick of a wild card race while the Giants are already playing out the string, which sets up an oddly lopsided but not entirely meaningless divisional finale. This one leans heavily on San Diego doing what good playoff teams do to bad ones — the numbers and the vibes both point that way. The Padres arrive with the majority of the watchability here: a 9.81 tNERD built on excellent bullpen work and above-average fielding, while the Giants check in at a middling 3.95, dragged down by shaky baserunning and a bullpen that's been below average. San Francisco's been officially eliminated from playoff contention for a fifth straight year, and their offense has been especially punchless against lefties this month, which is bad news against Robbie Ray tonight. Ray himself is a wrinkle — his surface numbers (11-8, 3.39 ERA) look solid, but his pNERD sits at a low 0.80, with a poor strike percentage and slow pace working against him. Anthony Molina, on the other side, is a near-total mystery statistically (pNERD of 0.00, no meaningful data), though he's been sharp in limited starts. Both teams enter on winning streaks, which adds a bit of juice, but overall this gNERD of 9.78 sits a shade below today's average, making it a watchable-but-skippable outing unless you're a Padres fan sweating the standings.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

This one's got a genuine debut storyline: a division race, a hot road team, and a rookie fireballer getting his first career start after a dominant relief stint. The gNERD of 15.42 sits well above both the historic average (10.81) and today's slate (10.95), driven mostly by a strong pitching matchup and two above-average offenses.

Jared Jones brings real stuff to the mound — 98.4 mph average velocity and a hefty whiff rate translate into a 10.33 pNERD, comfortably above today's average of 5.97, even though his surface-level ERA sits at 4.46. He's taking the mound for his 18th start with a 4.46 ERA over 78 2/3 innings, and most recently threw six scoreless innings against the Angels. Across the mound, Hagen Smith makes his first career start after debuting on August 9 and pitching excellently in short bursts, owning a 0.56 ERA with 23 strikeouts across 16 innings in relief appearances. No pNERD data exists yet for a starter role, but the bullpen numbers are eye-popping. Both lineups carry decent pop — White Sox tNERD of 8.36 edges Pittsburgh's 7.15 — and Pittsburgh has already taken both games of this series, including a 9-3 opener. Worth tuning in for the young arm alone.

A 38-year-old Jacob deGrom, still throwing 97, headlines a game that's genuinely worth carving out time for, even if the Mariners' anemic offense makes it a low-scoring affair on paper. DeGrom sits at a 11.01 pNERD — among the best you'll see today — thanks to elite strikeout stuff and a sparkling xFIP-, and his surface-level numbers (3.96 ERA) are actually underselling him. The underlying numbers suggest that deGrom's struggles are mostly just unluckiness, with a sterling 2.69 FIP lately, which lines up with the positive Luck component in his profile pointing toward better days ahead. Gilbert is no slouch either (7.74 pNERD, mid-90s heat), though he's been homer-prone lately — an unusually high 4.68 ERA and matching 4.69 FIP over his last 10 starts, with a 10.6% opponent barrel rate. Seattle's offense is the drag here, ranking near the bottom of the league in scoring, which explains their sub-2 tNERD. Texas brings more thump and a well-above-expectations Luck bump. With a 13.27 gNERD comfortably above the day's 10.95 average, this is a pitching-forward watch, not a slugfest — tune in for deGrom's stuff, not the scoreboard.

With an 8.16 gNERD, this lands below both the historical and today's averages; save your remote for something else.

Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

This is the top-rated game of the day, and it's not particularly close. A tightly-wound rubber match closes out the season series between the Cubs and Brewers, with Milwaukee riding a big NL Central cushion and eyeing a home sweep. Logan Henderson has quietly become one of the best young arms in baseball — sitting at 9-3 with a 2.48 ERA and a microscopic 0.79 WHIP across 83.1 innings — and his 8.73 pNERD backs that up, built on excellent strike-throwing and a stingy xFIP-. Gausman's been shakier of late but still owns a strong résumé; the two actually dueled six days ago, when these two starters combined for 14 innings and three earned runs in a 2-1 Cubs win. Both team offenses are lively — Chicago's power (led by a Pete Crow-Armstrong breakout) and Milwaukee's youthful, athletic lineup both grade out well in tNERD, with the Brewers boosted by strong fielding and bullpen work. At 18.03, this gNERD sits well above the historic 95th percentile and is the day's high mark, making it the easy pick if you only have time for one game.

Washington Nationals @ San Diego Padres, 1:10p

Summary

San Diego's playoff push meets Washington's fade in a series finale that's more watchable than the standings would suggest. The Padres are clinging to the final NL Wild Card spot, a game behind Arizona, while the Nationals limp into Petco Park trying to end a six-game losing streak in this finale, having let San Diego score four runs in the eighth to steal Tuesday's game. Walker Buehler continues his reclamation tour after bouncing between Boston and Philadelphia last year — his time in San Diego has "rehabilitated his career a bit", and he's been sharp lately, having allowed just one earned run on three hits over five innings against the Yankees in his last outing. His pNERD of 4.72 is middling but solidly above replacement-level theater. Opposite him, rookie lefty Jackson Kent is walking a tightrope: he's 1-3 with a 5.55 ERA across five starts since his August 12 debut, with 21 strikeouts and 19 walks — that command issue tanks his pNERD to 2.87. Team-wise, this is the real draw: San Diego's 9.64 tNERD is buoyed by a strong bullpen and above-average broadcast ratings, while Washington's 8.48 mark leans on youth and baserunning. Combined gNERD of 12.86 sits comfortably above the day's average — worth a look if you like playoff races with shaky rookie pitching thrown in.

Cincinnati Reds @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

The Dodgers roll out their best against a fading Reds club still clinging to faint wild-card hopes, and the pitching mismatch alone makes this worth a look. Los Angeles enters on a hot streak — the Dodgers have been playing their best baseball of the second half, winners of six straight and holding firm atop the NL West with an 88-57 record — while Cincinnati sits at 69-76, needing wins to keep any postseason hopes alive in September. Yamamoto is the headliner here, sporting a stellar 79 xFIP- and 8.29 pNERD (today's field averages just 4.76), backed by plus velocity and strikeout stuff; rookie Lowder, by contrast, is scuffling with a below-average xFIP- and a modest 3.74 pNERD, and carries a 5.43 ERA and 1.49 WHIP into this one. On the offensive side, the Dodgers' 7.85 tNERD (elite batting runs, strong bullpen) dwarfs Cincinnati's 5.11, though Elly De La Cruz's speed (88 runs, 25 steals) gives the Reds some chaos potential on the bases. At 12.50, this gNERD sits comfortably above the historical median and near today's average — solid, if unspectacular, watchability driven almost entirely by Yamamoto's arm and the Dodgers' late-season surge.

A pennant-race sleeper: the surging White Sox host a scrappy Pirates club, with just enough pitching intrigue to make it worth a glance. Chicago's stunning turnaround from three straight 100-loss seasons into an AL Central lead is the real headline here, and this game offers a decent, if unspectacular, viewing case, with today's 11.95 gNERD sitting a bit above the historic average of 10.81 but shy of today's own slate-topping games.

The White Sox carry the better team profile (8.41 tNERD), fueled by a young, cheap roster and solid barrel rates, though they've been quietly unlucky by -21 runs, suggesting better days could be ahead. Pittsburgh counters with excellent baserunning and a bullpen that's outperformed expectations, even if shaky fielding drags them down. On the mound, Davis Martin (4.90 pNERD) is returning from an IL stint for a right middle finger blister, activated on September 2, and is searching for his first win since mid-June. Lake Bachar (3.63 pNERD) brings solid strikeout stuff but shaky command. Both offenses have thump — Oneil Cruz's .506 xwOBA and Esmerlyn Valdez's .477 xwOBA give the Pirates real run-creation upside — so don't be shocked if this one gets loud.

Summary

Miami's tNERD of 9.21 stands out mostly because of good luck (they're outperforming their skill-based numbers, so some regression may be coming), a low payroll, and a young roster, while the Mets' tNERD of 5.65 is buoyed more by a strong bullpen and broadcast ratings than by actual hitting, which has been a genuine weakness. On the mound, it's a battle of the underwhelming: Stock's numbers are genuinely ugly — a 1.75 WHIP and 13 walks in just 26.1 innings, though his xFIP- suggests some bad luck is baked into that ugly line. Junk, meanwhile, has allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of his last five outings, but his NERD score is dragged down by a weak swinging-strike rate. New York enters having won the first two games of this series and won the first two games by scores of 9-4 and 7-5, so there's some series-finale drama, but at 10.47 this gNERD sits almost exactly at the historical median — competent, unremarkable, background-noise baseball.

Watch for Bennett's arm, not much else.

That's the kind of "watch the return" intrigue that can make an otherwise middling game worth a look, even though Gallen's rusty numbers (a 6.34 ERA before the IL stint) and his -1.47 xFIP- component drag his pNERD down to 3.00. Kansas City counters with Daniel Lynch IV, who's quietly been a stabilizer for a fading Royals club, and his absurdly quick 16.6-second pace (worth a full point in his pNERD) at least keeps things moving. The Diamondbacks arrive red-hot, having won four straight and pushing for a wild-card spot, while Kansas City has dropped seven of nine and is buried in last in the AL Central. At 8.43, the gNERD sits below both the historical and today's averages, so temper expectations, but Gallen's first outing back is worth a peek if you're near a TV anyway.

The tNERD marks are middling on both sides — Atlanta's 5.35 and Tampa Bay's 4.64 sit right around league-average, with the Rays' brutal barrel rate offset by battling underperformance (positive luck) that suggests better days ahead. A 9.86 gNERD lands below both the historic and today's-slate averages — competitive standings, unspectacular NERD math.

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

A tight NL Central race gives this one stakes, even if the arms on the mound are more workmanlike than dominant. Milwaukee holds a seven-game lead over Chicago, and with the Brewers looking to lock up the season series for tiebreaker purposes, this rematch of last week's series at Wrigley carries some late-season weight. Chicago won the most recent meeting 2-1, splitting a four-game series after Milwaukee had taken the middle two games by lopsided scores. Neither bullpen is fresh — Milwaukee's pen got overworked in a 12-8 loss in Cincinnati while Chicago's did the same in a 10-3 blowout in Miami, so neither unit arrives rested. Milwaukee is also without Brandon Woodruff and lost Quinn Priester for the season, forcing more bullpen reliance — but the Brewers' actual bullpen NERD component is strong, offsetting that. On the mound, Boyd and Gasser are both middling by NERD (3.92 and 4.74, roughly average for today's slate), though Gasser gets a bump from being unlucky this year. The real juice here is the offense and depth on both sides — this gNERD of 14.47 sits well above the historical average and near today's high end, making it one of the better watches on the board.

Cincinnati Reds @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

A rookie-adjacent ace with a wipeout slider takes the mound against baseball's best lineup, and the Reds' bullpen plan alone is worth the price of admission. This game rates 14.25 on the gNERD scale, comfortably above both the historic average (10.81) and today's slate average (11.60), and it's easy to see why once you look past the standings.

The headline is Chase Burns, whose 10.38 pNERD is well above the 95th percentile historically — he's been outstanding in 2026 with a 1.16 WHIP and a 28.9% strikeout rate that ranks among the best in the National League, fueled by upper-90s velocity and elite whiff rates. There's a wrinkle worth watching: a right elbow flexor strain briefly sidelined him this summer, and the Reds have been managing his workload carefully ever since, which explains why Terry Francona plans to piggyback Brandon Williamson behind Burns to keep his innings down. The Dodgers' response is a mystery-box TBD, reportedly journeyman/rookie fill-in Emmet Sheehan, whose stuff has been hittable in the minors.

Team-wise, the Dodgers (8.11 tNERD) bring a top-tier offense and bullpen, riding a four-game win streak, while the Reds (5.01 tNERD) are scuffling but oddly barrel the ball well. Not a must-watch pitching duel on paper, but Burns alone makes it worth tuning in early.

entry.content:

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Cincinnati Reds, 9:10a

Summary

A Brewers rotation arm chasing forearm-tightness redemption against a Reds bullpen that's been running on fumes — this one has enough moving parts to be worth a look, even if the pitching matchup is lopsided. Milwaukee's tNERD of 9.84 reflects a genuinely fun team: strong baserunning, a shutdown bullpen, and a young, cheap roster that overachieves its payroll. Cincinnati checks in lower at 5.10, dragged down by weak batting runs and bullpen performance, though positive luck suggests some regression upward is coming. On the mound, Kyle Harrison (pNERD 10.64) brings excellent strikeout stuff and a tidy xFIP-, but he's trying to bounce back from a disastrous start, having allowed nine runs on 10 hits -- including five homers -- in 3 2/3 innings against the Cubs, with pitch-tipping suspected as a culprit. Brady Singer (pNERD 4.72) is the weaker link statistically, though Cincinnati emptied its bullpen across Friday and Saturday, with every one of the team's eight active relievers pitching in one of those two games — meaning length from Singer matters more than usual. Today's gNERD of 15.15 sits well above both the historical and today's-slate averages, making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board despite Cincinnati's rough season.

Chicago Cubs @ Miami Marlins, 10:40a

Summary

A high-scoring gNERD matchup with a good story attached: Clay Holmes, back from a broken fibula, closing out a Cubs sweep bid against a fading Marlins team playing out the string. This one grades out well above both the historical and today's-game averages, and the details back it up.

Holmes was traded to Chicago in August and fractured his right fibula in May before joining the Cubs on an August 3 trade, with Sunday marking roughly his sixth start since being activated on August 8, having allowed just five earned runs across his last 29 innings. That kind of return-from-injury storyline, paired with a sinker-heavy, contact-suppressing profile, gives him a solid pNERD reading even if his strikeout stuff isn't loud. On the other side, Tyler Phillips brings a live arm — a 96.1 mph four-seamer and an 84.2 mph sweeper with a 33.3% whiff rate, with his splitter serving as his best weapon at a 34.4% whiff rate — though his control is shakier, evidenced by a WHIP that suggests he'll put runners on base.

The bigger draw is the Cubs' team profile, which ranks near the top of today's slate thanks to elite batting and fielding runs, offset some by a shaky bullpen. Miami's tNERD gets a boost from youth, payroll thrift, and positive luck (suggesting they've actually underperformed their true talent, not overperformed). The Cubs are chasing a wild card spot and can't afford to let a winnable series slip, backed by a road record that reflects genuine competence, while Miami is playing spoiler with the season effectively over. Good pitching, motivated Cubs, nothing at stake for Miami — a solid, watchable Sunday matchup.

New York Yankees @ San Diego Padres, 1:10p

Summary

I've got great material now. Let me write the summary.

A rubber match with legit wild-card stakes and a rematch of the Michael King trade, this one's got juice beyond the NERD math. Cole (7.66 pNERD) is the headliner here, still pumping mid-90s heat at 35 with elite command — he's been the more trustworthy arm in this series and his xFIP- of 86 backs it up. King (3.70 pNERD) is respectable but walk-prone; the walks are the difference between the two profiles, as King has issued roughly 3.5 free passes per nine while Cole sits near 1.9. San Diego's tNERD (9.36) is buoyed by a strong bullpen and fielding, plus it's simply a nice broadcast to watch, but the Padres are 3-7 in their last 10 and clinging to a wild-card spot, while the Yankees just won 5-1 to even the series. Petco Park's pitcher-friendly dimensions suggest a tight, low-scoring affair rather than a slugfest. At 14.35, the gNERD score sits comfortably above today's 11.55 average and well past the historical mean, making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board, even if the storyline outshines the raw stuff on a couple of these arms.

Washington arrives limping on a six-game road skid, but this is one of the higher gNERD scores on the board today, and both offenses have real thump behind them — Washington's baserunning has been outstanding all year, and the Dodgers' bat-driven attack ranks near the top of the NL. Wrobleski, an All-Star this season, returns to the rotation with a tidy strikeout rate and quick pace that pushes his pNERD to 6.70; Alvarez is coming off his best start of the season, a six-inning scoreless outing against Miami last Sunday, and will be making his first career start at Dodger Stadium, notably close to his hometown. Gavin Williams looks like a legitimate reason to tune in, even if the rest of this September getaway game between two fading-to-mediocre AL Central clubs isn't must-see TV. Williams brings a filthy arm to Progressive Field: he's 13-7 with a 3.81 ERA over 28 starts and 163 innings this season, striking out 11.98 batters per nine, and he's fresh off seven scoreless innings against Toronto on September 1 with a career-high 13 strikeouts. His pNERD of 12.78 is elite—well above today's average of 5.94 and in the 95th-percentile range historically—driven by a filthy xFIP and a positive luck value suggesting he's actually been slightly unlucky given his stuff. Jobe, on the other hand, is still finding his feet five starts into his return from Tommy John surgery, and his 4.76 pNERD reflects wildness (SwStr% and Strike% both below average) offset by big velocity and youth. Team-wise, Cleveland's 6.74 tNERD (payroll and age components doing heavy lifting) outpaces Detroit's middling 3.06, and the Guardians have dominated this season's series, winning 9 of 11 head-to-head meetings this season. With a gNERD of 13.67—comfortably above both the historical and today's averages—this is worth a look mostly for the pitching mismatch, even if the standings race has mostly evaporated for Detroit.

Tampa Bay Rays @ Texas Rangers, 11:35a

Summary

Good, I have enough. Now let me write the summary.

Rays lead AL East by four games with baseball's best record, but this is a series finale with mixed motivation levels — Tampa's already comfortable while Texas is scrapping for a wild-card spot. The pitching matchup rewards patience over power: Ian Seymour brings the higher pNERD by a wide margin thanks to excellent command indicators, though he's lost his last four decisions, most recently allowing three runs over 6.1 innings against the Mets. MacKenzie Gore counters with mid-90s velocity and a strikeout-heavy profile, backed by a strong recent stretch, though his control has been shaky.A tale of two seasons colliding in Arlington, with better pitching than the standings gap suggests. Tampa Bay arrives with baseball's best record and a four-game AL East cushion, while Texas is scrapping for wild-card life; that mismatch in stakes is offset by two lefties who make this more watchable than the records imply. Ian Seymour owns the far superior pNERD here, built on sharp command indicators (strong strike and swinging-strike rates translating into an xFIP- in the 80s), even though he enters 9-6 with a 4.21 ERA and the Rays have lost his last four starts, including a six-hit, three-run outing over 6.1 innings against the Mets. MacKenzie Gore brings mid-90s velocity and a strikeout-friendly profile, and has flashed swing-and-miss stuff with a strong recent run, a 2.77 ERA over his last seven starts, though his command lags Seymour's. Both team tNERDs sit near league-average, with Texas getting a lucky-team bump that suggests some regression could be coming. Today's slate averages 11.55, so this 12.74 gNERD lands comfortably above par—a solid, if unspectacular, pick.

Great matchup for pitching but a lopsided one for everything else, and a nice childhood-fandom subplot makes it worth a look even if the Angels are running on fumes. Paul Skenes carries an elite pNERD of 10.20 thanks to a filthy xFIP- of 79 and a mid-90s heater, but his last several outings tell a shakier story: over his last five starts he has allowed 17 earned runs in 24.2 innings, and he has cleared six innings once in six outings, and he enters on a seven-start winless streak after picking up a no-decision in his last start on Tuesday against San Francisco. Tolle, Boston's 23-year-old lefty and 2024 second-round pick, checks in with a robust 9.85 pNERD — he recorded a career-high 14 strikeouts over six innings against the Athletics on August 7, becoming the youngest Red Sox pitcher to reach that threshold since Roger Clemens. His secret sauce is elite command and swing-and-miss stuff for his age, not simply gaudy strikeout totals. Bradish, by contrast, limps in with a 2.57 pNERD, and has not earned a victory since July 22 and allowed 12 runs over his final 15 innings entering Sunday. Boston has been thoroughly outclassing Baltimore in this series — outscoring Baltimore 12-5 across the first three games — and looks poised for a sweep. Boston's tNERD (6.50) edges Baltimore's (5.72), buoyed by a strong bullpen and some positive regression luck. Not a marquee slugfest, but Tolle's emergence makes this a legitimate watch.

Both teams are middling on the tNERD side — sloppy fielding drags both down — with Seattle sitting a season-worst 11 games under .500 and seven back in the AL West. This is a pitching-matchup game, not a lineup one; watch it for Woo.

Both the Giants (59-84) and Mets (64-78) are playing out the string, but rookie lefty Cesar Perdomo gets his first career MLB start after a promising relief debut where he allowed only one run on a solo home run over four innings while striking out four hitters. He draws no pNERD score simply because there's no track record yet — pure lottery ticket. Christian Scott, on the other hand, brings real numbers: a strong strikeout rate and solid velocity give him a 5.77 pNERD, though his command has wobbled lately — his command has slipped, and over his last five starts he has allowed 17 earned runs in 25.1 innings, a 6.04 mark, while walking 14. Neither offense is scary — the Mets' batting runs are well below average and the Giants aren't running or fielding their way to relevance — though Rafael Devers and Luis Arraez remain worth watching in the box score. At 10.08 gNERD, this sits a bit below the historic average and squarely in the middle of today's slate — watchable mostly for Perdomo's debut and Scott's swing-and-miss stuff.

Minnesota's 3.22 tNERD is the drag on this one, hurt by shaky fielding and baserunning, and further complicated by a lineup that is walking out without Byron Buxton, Austin Martin, Joe Ryan, and Cole Sands, though it still has real pieces in Kody Clemens, Ryan Jeffers, and Trevor Larnach. Chicago, meanwhile, comes in with real momentum behind them — the White Sox will try to keep their power surge going after a 4-1 win in Friday's series opener, in which they hit three home runs.

On the mound, Taj Bradley is the reason to tune in, sporting a strong 7.20 pNERD thanks largely to elite velocity (97.2 mph, well above the pack) and useful strikeout stuff — he's compiled a 10–6 record with a 3.85 ERA, a 1.26 WHIP, and 178 strikeouts, ninth-most in MLB. Anthony Kay is the far weaker complementary arm at 2.50 pNERD, and he's winless in his past four starts, with a slower pace and shakier command. Overall gNERD of 10.58 sits almost exactly at the historic median — decent, unspectacular, worth a look mainly for Bradley and Chicago's offense.

I have enough here.

A wild-card scrap between a scuffling Toronto club and a Kansas City team playing out the string, with two veteran pitchers who've both seen better days. The Blue Jays are clawing for their playoat life while the Royals are just trying to spoil the party, and the pitching matchup does little to inspire confidence in either direction.

Toronto sits 13.5 games back in the division but is very much alive in the wild card conversation, having gone 21-13 since July 27, and they enter having gone 7-3 over their last ten games riding a three-game winning streak — including a Friday blowout where nine different Blue Jays recorded a hit. On the mound, Max Scherzer is the headline name but not the reason to tune in: Scherzer is 2-7 with a 6.16 ERA — a difficult stretch for a veteran who has been one of the game's most decorated starters, and his xFIP-backed pNERD of 1.37 reflects real skill decline, not just bad luck (well, actually some good luck, since his 23.0 luck score suggests he's earned an even worse line than his ERA shows). Seth Lugo is modestly more interesting statistically, his quick pace and respectable peripherals pushing him to a 4.14 pNERD, though he has struck out 118 batters but carries a 5.03 ERA of his own. Both teams' offenses and shaky bullpens (Kansas City's especially, a full two standard deviations below average) suggest a laugher is as likely as a pitcher's duel. At a 6.36 gNERD — well below both the historical and today's average — this one's a bottom-of-the-list watch unless you're a Jays fan sweating the standings.

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

Two aces, a division race, and a genuine ace-vs-ace duel make this the best watch on the board today. Chris Sale and Cristopher Sánchez sit at Nos. 3 and 2, respectively, in MLB.com's most recent NL Cy Young poll, and this is round two of their season series—their first meeting ended with Sánchez allowing three runs, all unearned, over six innings, while Sale countered with seven innings of one-run ball. The stakes are real too: the Braves and Phillies are entering a critical stretch with seven meetings in 10 games, and Atlanta currently holds a four-game lead in the NL East. Sale has been quietly dominant, having allowed more than three earned runs just once all season, with the Angels tagging him for six in four innings back in April, while Sánchez has been nails at home, going 11-1 with a 1.68 ERA in home starts this season. The gNERD of 15.75 sits in the upper tier both historically (95th percentile is 15.6) and among today's slate (season-high 15.75), driven almost entirely by two elite arms with xFIP- in the 60s and swinging-strike rates well above average. Neither team's offense is thrilling on paper, but with this pitching and this postseason context, that hardly matters.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:15p

Summary

Milwaukee's charging into Wrigley with the majors' best rookie storyline on the mound, and this one lands near the top of today's slate for good reason. Logan Henderson has been a revelation, carrying a 9-2 record, 2.48 ERA, and 3.29 FIP across 14 starts, and he's been remarkably stingy with free passes — a 2.48 ERA and 0.83 WHIP across 76.1 innings while walking just 14 batters all season against 86 strikeouts. His pNERD of 8.77 reflects that combination of elite command and swing-and-miss stuff, well above today's average. Gausman, by contrast, has been the definition of inconsistent since arriving from Toronto — a 3-1 record with a 5.14 ERA and 4.08 FIP over five Cubs starts, alternating rough outings with a couple of gems — though his pNERD still checks in at a respectable 6.77, boosted by some bad luck that suggests better days ahead. On the team side, Chicago's tNERD (10.44) is carried by standout batting and fielding runs, while Milwaukee's (9.82) leans on baserunning and a strong bullpen, though the Cubs' pen is a real liability. Combined, this gNERD of 17.90 sits comfortably above both the historic 95th percentile and today's field — genuinely one of the day's best watches.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

Tarik Skubal at Dodger Stadium against a Cardinals lineup missing key pieces is about as good a watchability bet as you'll find on the slate today. The Dodgers ace, now in his second month in LA after the trade-deadline blockbuster, has been every bit the marquee arm: Skubal has a 3.00 ERA and 37 strikeouts over 30 innings as a Dodger, and owns a 2.84 ERA with 153 strikeouts across 126.2 innings pitched overall this season. His last time out, he threw six innings against the Detroit Tigers, giving up one earned run while allowing four hits. His pNERD of 12.23 is driven by elite whiff and strike rates plus a stingy xFIP-, and it ranks near the top of today's pitcher scores. Opposite him is Quinn Mathews, making his fifth start for the Cardinals, sitting at 1-2 with a 5.03 ERA and 20 strikeouts in 19 2/3 innings — a rookie with no track record yet, hence the flat 0.00 pNERD. The Dodgers' offense (tNERD 8.16) and bullpen give them the clear team-level edge over St. Louis's older, lighter-payroll but well-fielding Cardinals (6.35). With a gNERD of 15.87, well above both the historic and today's averages, this is a legitimate top-of-the-slate watch, carried almost entirely by Skubal.

Miami Marlins @ Kansas City Royals, 4:40p

Summary

The Marlins try to complete a sweep in Kansas City, and Wacha's recent form makes that a tougher ask than the standings suggest. Kansas City hasn't lost a start from Wacha in more than three weeks, and he's riding real heat: his most recent start was his best of the season, working eight innings against Cleveland with four hits, no walks and a season-high 10 strikeouts. Alcantara, meanwhile, has been the opposite story—the Marlins have struggled to win with their ace on the mound, losing four straight starts he's made—even though his stuff remains loud, with a 97-plus mph fastball driving his pNERD edge.
